subject: Science
title: Mitosis and the cell cycle
reading_age_est: rough ARI grade 8.33 on 963 pupil-visible words; heuristic age guide 14.33 years, not a formal reading-age test
pupil_words: I am learning to order the cell cycle and explain why a cell makes two matching cells.
success_criteria: I can order interphase, four mitosis phases and cytokinesis.
I can show that the two new body cells have matching chromosome sets.
I can explain how mitosis helps growth or repair.

vocab.definition: the series of steps in which a cell grows and divides
vocab.example: The cell cycle includes interphase, mitosis and cytokinesis.

vocab.definition: the stage in which the cell grows and copies its DNA
vocab.example: The cell copies its DNA in interphase.

vocab.definition: the stage in which copied chromosomes separate into two nuclei
a structure of DNA that carries genes
vocab.example: Each new nucleus receives a matching set of chromosomes.

vocab.definition: the division of the cell after the nuclei form
vocab.example: Cytokinesis splits one cell into two.

vocab.definition: the mitosis phase when chromosomes condense
vocab.example: In prophase, chromosomes become easier to see.

vocab.definition: the mitosis phase when chromosomes line up in the middle
vocab.example: In metaphase, chromosomes form a line.

vocab.definition: the mitosis phase when the two copies of each chromosome are pulled to opposite ends
vocab.example: In anaphase, the two copies of each chromosome are pulled to opposite ends.

vocab.definition: the mitosis phase when two new nuclei form
vocab.example: In telophase, each set gains a nucleus.

worked_example.full: Interphase: copy DNA. Mitosis: prophase (condense), metaphase (line up), anaphase (the two copies of each chromosome are pulled to opposite ends), telophase (two nuclei). Cytokinesis: split the cell.
worked_example.faded: Interphase: copy DNA. Mitosis: prophase (condense), metaphase (line up), ________, telophase (two nuclei). Cytokinesis: split the cell.
worked_example.removed_step: Anaphase: the two copies of each chromosome are pulled to opposite ends.
worked_example.fade_next: Next lesson remove the metaphase cue as well; ask pupils to rebuild the sequence from the model before checking.

cfu.question: Show me: is DNA copied before, during or after mitosis?

hinge.question: A new body-cell model starts with six chromosomes. After DNA copying, mitosis and cell division, what should each daughter cell contain?

options.text: A. Half the original set, with just three chromosomes each.
options.diagnosis: Confuses body-cell mitosis with chromosome halving in meiosis.

options.text: B. Double the original set, with twelve chromosomes in each.
options.diagnosis: Counts the copied chromosomes before separation as the number retained by each daughter cell.

options.text: C. The same six-chromosome set as the original body cell.
D. No chromosomes, because the copies remain in one cell.
options.diagnosis: Assumes copied chromosomes stay in the parent cell instead of separating into two cells.

hinge.decision_rule: About 3 in 4 or more right → move on; otherwise re-model copying and splitting with two blue and two orange paper strips, then ask the parallel hinge. No automatic grade or saved response.
hinge.parallel_hinge: A different body-cell model starts with eight chromosomes. After ordinary mitosis and cell division, how many are in each daughter? Answer: eight, with a matching set.

misconceptions.misconception: Mitosis halves the chromosome number to make gametes.
misconceptions.spot: Pupil chooses A, the halved three-chromosome set.
misconceptions.correction: Contrast mitosis with meiosis: for this body-cell model, copy and separate so both cells keep the same chromosome set.

misconceptions.misconception: Mitosis alone is the whole cell split.
misconceptions.spot: Pupil chooses D, leaving copies in one cell.
misconceptions.correction: Point to the final cytokinesis arrow; move the two paper circles apart to represent two cells.

we_do.support: Use the full model beside the faded one. Point to the two nuclei before choosing the missing step.
we_do.stretch: Explain why swapping mitosis and DNA copying would break the model.

tiers.F: Order the three cards and show the same chromosome colours in each new cell.
tiers.M: Explain why each new cell has a matching chromosome set.
tiers.H: Predict what would happen to the sets if copied chromosomes did not separate evenly.

stems.H: If the copies did not separate evenly, then … because …

tiers.go_deeper: How do copy, separate and split work together when new cells are needed for repair?
tiers.early_finisher: Fault finder: compare two faulty models. One skips DNA copying; the other puts both copies of one chromosome in one nucleus. Find each first error and propose a repair.

adaptations.cognition_learning: Use three large cards with a four-phase mini-strip inside mitosis; remove the anaphase cue, then fade metaphase next lesson.
adaptations.communication_interaction: Give two quiet partner turns and the same speaking frame before any writing; accept point, sign or AAC for the explanation.
adaptations.semh: Check in before the top rung and hinge; offer an agreed pause and a one-step return without public correction.
adaptations.sensory_physical: Offer enlarged, high-contrast, easy-grip chromosome strips and a seated or standing choice; accept speech-to-text.
adaptations.eal: Pre-teach the science terms with diagram and example sentences; allow planning in any language and the same M/H scientific task with a speaking frame.

speaking_frames: First the cell …; then the chromosome sets …; last the cell …

ta_focus.i_do: “Watch the DNA copy. Point to where the two matching sets go.”
ta_focus.we_do: “You have the first and last steps. What might happen between them?”
ta_focus.independent: “Show me the last step you know. What does the model tell you next?”

prompt_ladder: Wait: count to five and watch for an independent move.
Point or gesture to the last complete card or model step.
Verbal cue: “What happened to the copied chromosomes?”
Model one move with one colour; pupil repeats with the other colour.
Finish one step together; then ask the pupil to try a fresh step alone.

F.q: Which step splits the whole cell?

M.q: Why do the daughter cells have matching sets?
M.a: DNA was copied and the matching chromosome sets separated into two nuclei.
It produces more body cells with matching chromosome sets.

H.q: What happens to the two copies of each chromosome during anaphase?
H.a: The two copies of each chromosome are pulled to opposite ends.

H.q: Why is the order copy, separate, split important?
H.a: The copies must exist before separation, and the cell divides after each nucleus has a set.

items: Mitosis — in anaphase the two copies of each chromosome are pulled to opposite ends

B. Double the original set, with twelve chromosomes in each.
C. The same six-chromosome set as the original body cell.
D. No chromosomes, because the copies remain in one cell.
interactions.answer_key: C. The same six-chromosome set as the original body cell. Teacher reads group response; no automatic grade.
